Before I alternate between eviscerating and commending this movie, please understand that it's a good movie overall. Keanu Reeves is a good dude that does his own stunts and spent hundreds of hours at the range to perfect his technique for this series, so I don't hold anything against him in the slightest. Plus, the series is directed by a stunt double from The Matrix (rather than the transgender abominations that slapped their "female" names on the trilogy), so it's not completely pozzed.

For the most part, this movie surpasses the average modern Hollywood film, which goes out of its way to sensationalize AR-15s, suppressors, and anything with a full auto function.

Starting with the good. From what I saw, the scenes in this movie use a realistic number of rounds prior to reloading. Most of the pistols used are fairly modern (10-15 round capacity), and nobody really exceeds that without a reload. The portion where the "sommelier" recommends weapons is also fairly well done. I'm not sure about the "ionized" thingamajigs he talks about at one point, but unlike most Hollywood actors, Keanu clearly shows he knows his way around a pistol/rifle. If he picks up a gun and has a free moment, John Wick typically either checks the chamber or ejects the mag to check how many rounds are left, before trying to take down three people at once. John Wick also maintains a "tacticool" pistol stance, which I've never tried at a range, but I'm sure is efficient for anyone trained with the weapon. Finally, any headshots typically occur after someone has been immobilized via hand-to-hand combat or a quick kneecapping. I say "typically" because there's about 50 headshots in the movie, so some might be completely unrealistic snipes that'd end up on a Call of Duty montage set to Skrillex. Which, via that reference, may just prove how out of touch I am with Gen Zyklon's fads.

Here comes the "bad", which I hate to rattle off because this was a good action movie, moreso given how bad the industry has become. I assumed they'd be using "blank" rounds to still produce a muzzle flash and recoil, but some scenes (especially with rifles and the Benelli shotgun) looked like characters simply pointed the guns higher periodically. I'm not familiar with the recoil compensation on a semi-auto shotgun, but John Wick looked like he didn't even flinch whenever he fired it. Next, near the end where the mercenaries are chasing John, their rifles are set to full-auto. The Army, to my knowledge, normally doesn't go above burst unless it's an LMG or some variant that can be mounted before firing. So why are a bunch of suit-wearing assholes running around on full-auto to kill one guy? My last gripe is with suppressors. First of all, the DEAF character is using one. But more importantly, when John Wick and that Cassian guy are shooting at each other with "suppressed" pistols in a busy subway corridor, nobody notices. This could be a completely "meta" commentary on how anyone in a big city is completely oblivious to the world around them, but unless they're firing .22 subsonic ammo, that's still going to be fairly loud.

As I noted before, still a good movie. And if you're looking for the best revenge story for a dead puppy, start at the 1st one. But given how much time Keanu spent at the range to prepare for this role, I just wish he would have passed some of the knowledge on to the writing and directing staff.
